lore.tribalpower.tablet.0.title: Pad-keepers' Hearth
lore.tribalpower.tablet.0.text: We never called it dirt. We called it what was left, and we kept it warm. When the ground fell away we carried it in baskets, a pad at a time, and set a hearth on every pad we saved. Feed the hearth bread and moss. It remembers who fed it.
lore.tribalpower.tablet.1.title: Grit-singers' Mesh
lore.tribalpower.tablet.1.text: The mesh does not find the ore. The mesh gives the ore somewhere to land. Sing low over raw stone and it loosens; sing lower and it shatters into echo. Our meshes still hang in the halls, humming to nothing. Bring them ore and they will hum to you.
lore.tribalpower.tablet.2.title: Rootbinders' Rope
lore.tribalpower.tablet.2.text: Roots are the only rope the void respects. We planted the first anchors on the falling islands and bound them island to island, root to root. Half of them held. Plant a sapling in the March soil and you will feel it pull toward the others.
lore.tribalpower.tablet.3.title: Edge-walkers' Boots
lore.tribalpower.tablet.3.text: Boots first. Then the bridge. Then the courage; it arrives on its own. We walked the rift edge where the thread frayed thinnest and set footholds for the rest. A foothold is iron, leather and a promise not to look down.
lore.tribalpower.tablet.4.title: Drumhearts' Beat
lore.tribalpower.tablet.4.text: The drum is not loud. The drum is steady. Be the drum. One beat a breath apart, and the copper answers; miss a beat and it forgets you. Every engine in the March still keeps our time. Strike, wait, strike. That is the whole of it.
lore.tribalpower.tablet.5.title: Pattern-weavers' Song
lore.tribalpower.tablet.5.text: A factory is a song that has stopped needing the singer. We wrote the timings on clock-wheels and moth dust and let the Loom carry the tune. When the Cut came the songs kept playing. Some are playing still. Listen for the click before the hum.
lore.tribalpower.tablet.6.title: Colony-keepers' Hive
lore.tribalpower.tablet.6.text: You do not own a hive. You are on good terms with it. Offer honey, plant the March flowers, and the swarm will route Pulse through the comb for you. Take without asking and the comb goes quiet. It is very patient about this.
lore.tribalpower.tablet.7.title: Seal-carvers' Rite
lore.tribalpower.tablet.7.text: Spirit goes where it is asked politely and stays where it is fed. A seal is a polite request carved in stone. A brazier is the meal. We cut blank seals by the thousand before the Cut, and asked for far too much. Ask for a little. Feed it well.
lore.tribalpower.tablet.8.title: Loom-stitchers' Thread
lore.tribalpower.tablet.8.text: The Loom was never one thread. It was nine agreeing. We held the Spindle and stitched the tribes' strands into one cloth over the sky. When eight pulls became eight arguments, the cloth tore along our seam. We are still stitching. Bring crystal. Bring thread.
lore.tribalpower.tablet.9.title: The Cut
lore.tribalpower.tablet.9.text: No one struck the Loom. It was pulled from nine sides until one strand gave, and then the rest went like a rope through a hand. The continents fell in the space of a drum-roll. What did not fall drifted into the March and sank slow. Nine tribes, one hall, no one to blame.
lore.tribalpower.tablet.10.title: The Unsung
lore.tribalpower.tablet.10.text: A drum was carried out of every falling camp so the beat would not stop. The last drum was carried into the circle and no one was left to strike it. Its keeper went hollow waiting. Wake it with the four-beat and it will rise to be struck. Sneak when it beats. Resync it when it goes silent. It only wants the rhythm back.
lore.tribalpower.tablet.11.title: The March
lore.tribalpower.tablet.11.text: The March is where the thread frayed thinnest and the fallen ground came to rest. Halls lie sunk to the lintel; camps keep time with no one at the drum; crystal grows where the Loom's tension still pools. Walk it with a full Pulse Cell and a steady hand. Everything here still answers a beat.

dialogue.tribalpower.soil.lore.2: Our craft is keeping: hearths, caches, the slow warm things. Anyone can take. Keeping is the work.
dialogue.tribalpower.soil.request.given: Good. Small work, but the pads are made of small work.
dialogue.tribalpower.soil.request.active: It is not done yet. The hearth is patient; so am I.
dialogue.tribalpower.soil.request.done: That is one more thing kept. The hearth remembers it, and so do the Pad-keepers.
dialogue.tribalpower.soil.quest.1: First be known at our hearth. Bring what you bring until we call you friend.
dialogue.tribalpower.soil.quest.2: The pads are thin at the edge. Bring me sixteen Moss Blocks and we will thicken them.
dialogue.tribalpower.soil.quest.3: Things come out of the dark to scratch at the pads. Turn eight of them back, near our fires.
dialogue.tribalpower.soil.quest.4: Sing a rite at a brazier within our camp. The pads listen better when they are sung to.
dialogue.tribalpower.soil.quest.5: Make our dish, the Keeper's Root Mash, and bring it to me warm. A pad is only a pad until someone eats on it.
dialogue.tribalpower.soil.quest.6: There is a pad we could not save: the Trampled Ring on the steppe. The herd that died there still runs. Lay Shank Sinew on its altar, face the Stampede Spirit, and bring the pad quiet.
questline.tribalpower.step.trial.soil: Face the Stampede Spirit at the Trampled Ring.
item.tribalpower.relic.soil.desc: A coal from the first hearth, still warm after all this time.
dialogue.tribalpower.stone.stranger.1: Ore does not fall into a mesh by luck. Neither does trust.
dialogue.tribalpower.stone.stranger.2: Bring grit, or ore, or a charged cell, and set it on the hearth. Then we talk.
dialogue.tribalpower.stone.greet: You hear that? The mesh is singing. Speak up over it.
dialogue.tribalpower.stone.done: The stone rings your name now. That is not a thing we say to many.
dialogue.tribalpower.stone.lore.1: The mesh does not find the ore. It gives the ore somewhere to land. We sing so it lands where we can reach it.
dialogue.tribalpower.stone.lore.2: Every song has a pitch the stone likes. We spent lifetimes finding it. You may borrow it, if you carry your share.
dialogue.tribalpower.stone.request.given: Do it well or do it twice. Stone does not care which.
dialogue.tribalpower.stone.request.activ: Still ringing in my ear, that one. Finish it.
dialogue.tribalpower.stone.request.done: Well landed. The Grit-singers will remember the pitch of that.
dialogue.tribalpower.stone.quest.1: Stand at our hearth until we know your pitch. Friend first.
dialogue.tribalpower.stone.quest.2: Eight Iron Grit, sung out of the stone yourself. I will hear if it was bought.
dialogue.tribalpower.stone.quest.3: The dark sends things that grind on our meshes. Break eight of them near our hearths.
dialogue.tribalpower.stone.quest.4: Perform a rite at a brazier in our camp. The stone under it will answer if you did it right.
dialogue.tribalpower.stone.quest.5: Cook Grit-baked Bread and bring it. It is terrible. We love it.
dialogue.tribalpower.stone.quest.6: In the Crystal Fields something sings back at our meshes, wrong: the Singing Fracture. Lay Prism Carapace on its altar, face the Prism Serpent, and set the pitch straight.
questline.tribalpower.step.trial.stone: Still the Prism Serpent at the Singing Fracture.
item.tribalpower.relic.stone.desc: A shard that hums the pitch the Grit-singers spent lifetimes finding.
dialogue.tribalpower.sprout.stranger.1: Roots first. Everything else can wait for roots.
dialogue.tribalpower.sprout.stranger.2: Plant something, or bring a seed, and set it by the hearth. That is how a stranger stops being one.
dialogue.tribalpower.sprout.greet: Roots holding today. Yours too, I hope.
dialogue.tribalpower.sprout.done: You are woven in now. Pull, and the whole hedge feels it. So do we.
dialogue.tribalpower.sprout.lore.1: Roots are the only rope the void respects. When everything fell we tied it back with living things.
dialogue.tribalpower.sprout.lore.2: We bind, we cut, we bind again. A hedge that never gets cut is just a wall that will not hold.
dialogue.tribalpower.sprout.request.give: Good. A root at a time, that is how anything grows.
dialogue.tribalpower.sprout.request.acti: It is still growing, that work. Give it water.
dialogue.tribalpower.sprout.request.done: Rooted. The Rootbinders count that as ours now, and yours.
dialogue.tribalpower.sprout.quest.1: Come to the hearth as a stranger and leave as a friend. Roots take time.
dialogue.tribalpower.sprout.quest.2: Twelve Spirit Reed, cut by your own hand. The hedges want thickening before the dark season.
dialogue.tribalpower.sprout.quest.3: Things chew on the roots at night. Eight of them, cut back, near our fires.
dialogue.tribalpower.sprout.quest.4: Sing a rite at a brazier in our camp. The reeds lean to whoever sings to them.
dialogue.tribalpower.sprout.quest.5: Bring Rootbinder Rice, hot. Nothing binds a hedge like a shared bowl.
dialogue.tribalpower.sprout.quest.6: At the Drowned Root in the Reed Fen something has grown that should not have. Lay Reed Fangs on its altar, face the Bog Matriarch, and cut her out.
questline.tribalpower.step.trial.sprout: Cut out the Bog Matriarch at the Drowned Root.
item.tribalpower.relic.sprout.desc: A knot of living root, still green, that remembers being tied to the world.
dialogue.tribalpower.claw.stranger.1: Boots off the bridge. You have not earned the bridge.
dialogue.tribalpower.claw.stranger.2: Bring a hide, a claw, or a good meal to the hearth. Then we will see about the bridge.
dialogue.tribalpower.claw.greet: Still standing. Good. So is the bridge.
dialogue.tribalpower.claw.done: You walked the edge and came back. That is all we have ever asked of anyone. Welcome, Edge-walker.
dialogue.tribalpower.claw.lore.1: Boots first. Then the bridge. Then the courage; it arrives on its own. We walk the edges no one else will.
dialogue.tribalpower.claw.lore.2: We hunt where the ground stops. What we bring back keeps the other camps fed. They pretend not to notice.
dialogue.tribalpower.claw.request.given: Do not come back with excuses. Come back with the thing.
dialogue.tribalpower.claw.request.active: Not done. The edge does not wait, and neither do I.
dialogue.tribalpower.claw.request.done: Clean. The Edge-walkers saw that, and we do not forget who walks well.
dialogue.tribalpower.claw.quest.1: Prove you can stand at our hearth without falling off it. Friend first.
dialogue.tribalpower.claw.quest.2: Six March Leather, cut by you. If it smells of a shop I will know.
dialogue.tribalpower.claw.quest.3: Hunt. Eight of the dark's things, near our fires, and bring nothing back but the story.
dialogue.tribalpower.claw.quest.4: A rite at a brazier in our camp. Even the edge likes a song before a jump.
dialogue.tribalpower.claw.quest.5: Cook Edge-walker Jerky and bring it. We eat before we jump, never after.
dialogue.tribalpower.claw.quest.6: At the Roost on the highlands something waits that has thrown better walkers than you. Lay Storm Wings on its altar, face the Storm Roc, and do not be thrown.
questline.tribalpower.step.trial.claw: Bring down the Storm Roc at the Roost.
item.tribalpower.relic.claw.desc: The last nail of the first bridge, carried by whoever walked it furthest.
dialogue.tribalpower.spark.stranger.1: You are off the beat. Everyone is, at first.
dialogue.tribalpower.spark.stranger.2: Bring coal, or a charged cell, or anything that burns, and lay it on the hearth. Find the beat.
dialogue.tribalpower.spark.greet: Steady. Steady. There it is. Good to see you.
dialogue.tribalpower.spark.done: You kept time with us through all of it. That makes you a Drumheart, whatever your hands were born as.
dialogue.tribalpower.spark.lore.1: The drum is not loud. The drum is steady. Be the drum. That is the whole of it, and it took us generations.
dialogue.tribalpower.spark.lore.2: We keep the tempo the machines follow. Lose the beat and the whole camp stutters. Keep it and nothing stops.
dialogue.tribalpower.spark.request.given: On the beat, now. Not before, not after.
dialogue.tribalpower.spark.request.activ: You dropped the beat on that one. Pick it up.
dialogue.tribalpower.spark.request.done: On the beat. The Drumhearts heard that, every one of us.
dialogue.tribalpower.spark.quest.1: Learn our tempo at the hearth first. Friend, then the rest.
dialogue.tribalpower.spark.quest.2: Four Attuned Echo. Not bought. Sung out of the stone at a proper tempo.
dialogue.tribalpower.spark.quest.3: The dark comes on its own rhythm. Break eight of its things near our fires, on ours.
dialogue.tribalpower.spark.quest.4: A rite at a brazier in our camp. Do it in time and you will feel the whole camp lean in.
dialogue.tribalpower.spark.quest.5: Cook Drumheart Chili and bring it hot. We eat fast. The beat does not wait.
dialogue.tribalpower.spark.quest.6: At the Slag Throne in the Ember Wastes something keeps a beat that is not ours. Lay Magma Scales on its altar, face the Slag Titan, and stop it.
questline.tribalpower.step.trial.spark: Stop the Slag Titan at the Slag Throne.
item.tribalpower.relic.spark.desc: A hand-drum whose skin has never once lost the beat.
dialogue.tribalpower.clock.stranger.1: You are a variable. We do not like variables.
dialogue.tribalpower.clock.stranger.2: Redstone, gears, anything that ticks: set it on the hearth and become a constant.
dialogue.tribalpower.clock.greet: Pattern holds. You are in it, for now. What do you need?
dialogue.tribalpower.clock.done: The pattern has a place for you now, and it does not have a place for many. Do not waste it.
dialogue.tribalpower.clock.lore.1: A factory is a song that has stopped needing the singer. We are the singers who taught it to stop.
dialogue.tribalpower.clock.lore.2: Every camp runs on something we laid out. They forget that. The pattern does not.
dialogue.tribalpower.clock.request.given: A small change to the pattern. Make it exactly.
dialogue.tribalpower.clock.request.activ: Incomplete. The pattern is waiting on you.
dialogue.tribalpower.clock.request.done: Exact. The Pattern-weavers note it, and we note everything.
dialogue.tribalpower.clock.quest.1: Be a constant at our hearth first. Friend standing.
dialogue.tribalpower.clock.quest.2: Bring a Clock. Any Clock. We want to see what the outside keeps time by.
dialogue.tribalpower.clock.quest.3: Eight of the dark's things, broken near our fires. Remove the variables.
dialogue.tribalpower.clock.quest.4: A rite at a brazier in our camp. Rites are patterns too, older than ours.
dialogue.tribalpower.clock.quest.5: Cook a Pattern Tart and bring it. Yes, it has a pattern. No, you will not see it.
dialogue.tribalpower.clock.quest.6: At the Tide Stone in the Shallows something has learned our pattern and runs it wrong. Lay Brine Fangs on its altar, face the Tide Drummer, and correct it.
questline.tribalpower.step.trial.clock: Stop the Tide Drummer at the Tide Stone.
item.tribalpower.relic.clock.desc: A gear that turns without a sound, taken from the first machine that stopped needing its singer.
dialogue.tribalpower.swarm.stranger.1: Slowly. The hive is watching. So are we.
dialogue.tribalpower.swarm.stranger.2: Honey, comb, or wax on the hearth, and the hive will stop watching so hard.
dialogue.tribalpower.swarm.greet: The hive says you are fine. The hive is usually right.
dialogue.tribalpower.swarm.done: The hive calls you one of its own, and we do not argue with the hive. Colony-keeper.
dialogue.tribalpower.swarm.lore.1: You do not own a hive. You are on good terms with it. Everything we know comes from that one sentence.
dialogue.tribalpower.swarm.lore.2: Bees, cells, camps, tribes. Keep the terms good and the whole thing hums. Break them and you will hear it.
dialogue.tribalpower.swarm.request.given: For the hive. It will know if you did not.
dialogue.tribalpower.swarm.request.activ: The hive has not heard it finished. Neither have I.
dialogue.tribalpower.swarm.request.done: The hive is pleased. So are the Colony-keepers, which is nearly the same thing.
dialogue.tribalpower.swarm.quest.1: Be on good terms with the hearth first. Friend.
dialogue.tribalpower.swarm.quest.2: Two Honey Blocks. Whole. The hive wants to see you can keep a thing intact.
dialogue.tribalpower.swarm.quest.3: The dark comes for the hives at night. Eight of its things, near our fires.
dialogue.tribalpower.swarm.quest.4: A rite at a brazier in our camp. The bees dance to it. Watch them.
dialogue.tribalpower.swarm.quest.5: Cook a Honeycake and bring it. Do not eat it on the way. The hive will know.
dialogue.tribalpower.swarm.quest.6: At the Cairn Ring in the Snow Fields the cold has taken a hive and turned it. Lay Rime Mandibles on its altar, face the Cairn Wight, and win the hive back.
questline.tribalpower.step.trial.swarm: Scatter the Cairn Wight at the Cairn Ring.
item.tribalpower.relic.swarm.desc: A cap of golden wax the hive gave, not sold, to one it calls its own.
dialogue.tribalpower.sigil.stranger.1: Ask politely. Everything here was asked for politely.
dialogue.tribalpower.sigil.stranger.2: Chalk, a seal, or spirit in any shape, laid on the hearth: that is how you ask.
dialogue.tribalpower.sigil.greet: Spirit is fed and staying. Good day for asking things. Ask.
dialogue.tribalpower.sigil.done: The seals know your hand now. Carve carefully; they will answer whatever you ask.
dialogue.tribalpower.sigil.lore.1: Spirit goes where it is asked politely and stays where it is fed. We carve the asking and we tend the feeding.
dialogue.tribalpower.sigil.lore.2: Every seal is a question. Most people carve demands. That is why most seals fail.
dialogue.tribalpower.sigil.request.activ: The question is still open. Close it.
dialogue.tribalpower.sigil.request.done: Answered. The Seal-carvers keep a ledger of answers, and yours is in it.
dialogue.tribalpower.sigil.quest.1: Be known at the hearth first. Ask often; friend comes.
dialogue.tribalpower.sigil.quest.2: Carve a Spirit Seal and bring it to me. I will read what you asked of it.
dialogue.tribalpower.sigil.quest.3: The dark's things come to break seals. Break eight of them first, near our fires.
dialogue.tribalpower.sigil.quest.4: A rite at a brazier in our camp. Watch what the seals do when the rite lands.
dialogue.tribalpower.sigil.quest.5: Cook Seal-carver's Broth and bring it. Spirit stays where it is fed, and so do Elders.
dialogue.tribalpower.sigil.quest.6: At the Sealed Gate on Glimmer Ridge something is unmaking our seals from the inside. Lay Sentinel Sigils on its altar, face the Vault Sentinel, and ask it to stop. Politely, then otherwise.
questline.tribalpower.step.trial.sigil: Still the Vault Sentinel at the Sealed Gate.
item.tribalpower.relic.sigil.desc: A seal carved as a question, which spirit has never once refused to answer.
dialogue.tribalpower.spindle.stranger.1: One thread. That is what you are, to the Loom. Do not be offended.
dialogue.tribalpower.spindle.stranger.2: Bring thread, a crystal, or thistle, and set it on the hearth. Threads become cloth by being near other threads.
dialogue.tribalpower.spindle.greet: The Loom holds. Nine threads, still agreeing. Well, eight and a half.
dialogue.tribalpower.spindle.done: Nine agreeing. You made the ninth hold. Whatever else you do, the Loom-stitchers will say that of you.
dialogue.tribalpower.spindle.lore.1: The Loom was never one thread. It was nine agreeing. When they stopped agreeing, everything you see fell.
dialogue.tribalpower.spindle.lore.2: We stitch what is left. We stitch the tribes to each other when they will let us. Mostly they will not.
dialogue.tribalpower.spindle.request.giv: A stitch. Small, but every cloth is small stitches.
dialogue.tribalpower.spindle.request.act: That stitch is loose. Pull it tight.
dialogue.tribalpower.spindle.request.don: Tight. The Loom-stitchers felt it, and the cloth is stronger by one.
dialogue.tribalpower.spindle.quest.1: Be a thread at our hearth first, then a friend.
dialogue.tribalpower.spindle.quest.2: Four March Crystal, unbroken. The Loom needs something to hold its tension.
dialogue.tribalpower.spindle.quest.3: The dark pulls threads. Eight of its things, near our fires, before they pull more.
dialogue.tribalpower.spindle.quest.4: A rite at a brazier in our camp. Feel the Loom take up the slack when it lands.
dialogue.tribalpower.spindle.quest.5: Cook Loom-thread Noodles. Nine threads in the bowl, agreeing. Bring it before they stop.
dialogue.tribalpower.spindle.quest.6: The Unsung is the thread that would not agree. Play the four-beat on the Silent Drum in the Drum Circle, face it, and make the ninth hold.
questline.tribalpower.step.trial.spindle: Still The Unsung at the Drum Circle.
item.tribalpower.relic.spindle.desc: A thread of the Loom that agreed, in the end, to hold.
block.tribalpower.guardian_altar.desc: A guardian's calling stone. Lay its biome's reagent on it, on the cap, between four candles.
message.tribalpower.guardian_altar.wants: The %s answers %s %s laid on this altar.
message.tribalpower.guardian_altar.no_al: This altar has no cap or candles. A guardian rises only from its circle.
message.tribalpower.guardian_altar.resti: The altar is still warm. It will answer again in about %s minutes.
message.tribalpower.guardian_altar.no_ro: There is no room above the altar for the guardian to rise.
item.tribalpower.rite_ninth_agreement.de: At a Loom circle, with all nine relics on you, the Loom agrees again.
message.tribalpower.rite.ninth_agreement: Nine threads agree. The March answers your voice.
The Loom will not agree while a thread is missing. Carry all nine relics.
The Loom already holds your agreement.
message.tribalpower.ninth_agreement.worl: %s has made the Ninth Agreement. Nine threads hold.
item.tribalpower.slag_core.desc: What the Slag Titan left behind. Loom Thread turns it to Resonant Cores; all eight make the last rite.
The Slag Titan cracks open. Its slag runs molten: keep out of the rings, and sneak when it slams.
The slag heaves and stands. The Slag Titan rises from its throne.
The Slag Titan cools and stills. The ash keeps a proper beat again.
item.tribalpower.fen_heart.desc: What the Bog Matriarch left behind. Loom Thread turns it to Resonant Cores; all eight make the last rite.
message.tribalpower.guardian.bog_matriar: The Bog Matriarch's roots go deep. Her snares poison now, and the fen sends her stalkers.
The fen boils. The Bog Matriarch rises from the drowned root.
The Bog Matriarch sinks. The roots of the fen grow straight.
item.tribalpower.cairn_stone.desc: What the Cairn Wight left behind. Loom Thread turns it to Resonant Cores; all eight make the last rite.
message.tribalpower.guardian.cairn_wight: The Cairn Wight's breath goes to the bone. Stand behind it; the crawlers come.
The cairns lift and turn. The Cairn Wight rises from the ring.
The Cairn Wight scatters into stones. Under them, the hive begins to hum.
item.tribalpower.prism_core.desc: What the Prism Serpent left behind. Loom Thread turns it to Resonant Cores; all eight make the last rite.
message.tribalpower.guardian.prism_serpe: The Prism Serpent splits its song. Two bolts for every one: keep moving.
The crystal sings one wrong note. The Prism Serpent rises from the fracture.
The Prism Serpent shatters. The crystal fields sing in tune.
item.tribalpower.vault_seal.desc: What the Vault Sentinel left behind. Loom Thread turns it to Resonant Cores; all eight make the last rite.
message.tribalpower.guardian.vault_senti: The Vault Sentinel wards itself. Wait for the light to fade before you strike.
The seals on the gate go dark. The Vault Sentinel steps out.
The Vault Sentinel kneels and is still. The seals answer again.
item.tribalpower.tide_shell.desc: What the Tide Drummer left behind. Loom Thread turns it to Resonant Cores; all eight make the last rite.
message.tribalpower.guardian.tide_drumme: The Tide Drummer changes tempo. The tide pulls harder; hold the shore.
The tide draws back and the drum begins. The Tide Drummer rises.
The Tide Drummer's beat stops. The tide keeps the pattern it was given.
item.tribalpower.herd_horn.desc: What the Stampede Spirit left behind. Loom Thread turns it to Resonant Cores; all eight make the last rite.
message.tribalpower.guardian.stampede_sp: The Stampede Spirit runs blind. Step aside, and the gnashers come up out of the ground.
The ground shakes with hooves that are not there. The Stampede Spirit rises.
The Stampede Spirit slows, and stops, and is dust. The lost pad is quiet.
item.tribalpower.storm_plume.desc: What the Storm Roc left behind. Loom Thread turns it to Resonant Cores; all eight make the last rite.
message.tribalpower.guardian.storm_roc.p: The Storm Roc calls its storm. Lightning follows its swoops now.
message.tribalpower.guardian.storm_roc.r: The wind drops, then screams. The Storm Roc falls out of the storm.
message.tribalpower.guardian.storm_roc.f: The Storm Roc falls from its storm. The edge is yours to walk.
dialogue.tribalpower.choice.festival_fea: I'd be glad to join the feast.
dialogue.tribalpower.soil.festival: It is the Day of Pads. Every pad we ever carried is warm today, and so is the hearth. Sit. Eat.
dialogue.tribalpower.soil.festival.thank: Eat well. That is what the day is for.
dialogue.tribalpower.stone.festival: Ringing Day. Every mesh in camp is tuned and the whole hill hums. Even I am cheerful. Do not get used to it.
dialogue.tribalpower.stone.festival.than: Good. Now go and hear the meshes ring.
dialogue.tribalpower.sprout.festival: Binding Day. We cut the hedges this morning and tie them tonight, and everyone eats in between. You too.
dialogue.tribalpower.sprout.festival.tha: Rooted. Eat, and stay for the tying.
dialogue.tribalpower.claw.festival: Edge Day. Every walker who came back is at this fire, and tonight we jump for the ones who did not. Eat first.
dialogue.tribalpower.claw.festival.thank: Eat. Then walk the edge with us.
dialogue.tribalpower.spark.festival: Tempo Day! Every drum in camp on one beat from dawn to dawn. Feel it? Good. Eat something before you drop.
dialogue.tribalpower.clock.festival: The Turning. The whole pattern runs one loop today and then rests. Even a factory has a holiday. Eat; it is scheduled.
dialogue.tribalpower.clock.festival.than: Exactly. Eat, then rest. It is in the pattern.
dialogue.tribalpower.swarm.festival: Hive Day. The hives are opened and the comb goes round, and the bees are told what we owe them. Eat your share.
dialogue.tribalpower.swarm.festival.than: Good terms. Eat, and thank the hive.
dialogue.tribalpower.sigil.festival: The Asking. Every seal in camp is re-carved today, politely, and spirit is fed until it purrs. Eat; you are being fed too.
dialogue.tribalpower.sigil.festival.than: Well asked. Eat, and mind the seals.
dialogue.tribalpower.spindle.festival: Agreeing Day. Nine threads, one cloth, one meal. Every tribe is invited; most do not come. You did. Eat.
dialogue.tribalpower.spindle.festival.th: Nine agreeing, for one meal at least. Eat.
message.tribalpower.surge.begins: The ley surges: every %s thread runs bright.
message.tribalpower.surge.ends: The surge fades and the threads settle.
message.tribalpower.surge.sickness: The ground sways under you: a bare crossing in a surge. Step off it.
message.tribalpower.festival.begins: It is the %s's festival day. Their camp is open to friends.
message.tribalpower.festival.joined: You join the %s's feast. The Elder presses two bowls into your hands.
message.tribalpower.festival.rite: The %s cheer the rite: festival thanks.
message.tribalpower.festival.feast: You eat at the %s's table on their day.
lore.tribalpower.spirit.ember_wastes.1: The ash was a forest once. The Drumhearts say it still keeps time, if you put your ear to the ground.
lore.tribalpower.spirit.ember_wastes.2: Nothing here is dead. It is waiting for a beat it can agree with.
lore.tribalpower.spirit.ember_wastes.3: The Slag Throne was a hearth, before it was a throne. Fire remembers what it was fed.
lore.tribalpower.spirit.reed_fen.1: The reeds are ropes the Rootbinders tied when the ground fell. Pull one and the whole fen feels it.
lore.tribalpower.spirit.reed_fen.2: Every drowned root was a road once. Walk them at low mist and you can still see the way.
lore.tribalpower.spirit.reed_fen.3: The Matriarch was a Rootbinder. She held on too long.
lore.tribalpower.spirit.snow_fields.1: Under the cairns the hives sleep. Hum to them and they hum back, slowly.
lore.tribalpower.spirit.snow_fields.2: The whiteout is not weather. It is the field forgetting where it ends.
lore.tribalpower.spirit.snow_fields.3: Every cairn marks a walker who chose the snow over the edge. The Edge-walkers do not speak of them.
lore.tribalpower.spirit.crystal_fields.1: The crystal sings what the Grit-singers taught the stone. Some of it is out of tune now.
lore.tribalpower.spirit.crystal_fields.2: A glimmer storm is the field remembering the Loom, all at once, for a little while.
lore.tribalpower.spirit.crystal_fields.3: The Serpent was born of a wrong note held too long. Sing over it.
lore.tribalpower.spirit.glimmer_ridge.1: The gate was sealed from the inside. The Seal-carvers do not say by whom.
lore.tribalpower.spirit.glimmer_ridge.2: Everything on the ridge is asked, not taken. The vault knows the difference.
lore.tribalpower.spirit.glimmer_ridge.3: Spirit stays where it is fed. Something under the ridge has been feeding it for a very long time.
lore.tribalpower.spirit.shallows.1: The tide keeps a pattern the Pattern-weavers laid down. It has not missed a beat in an age.
lore.tribalpower.spirit.shallows.2: Under the shallows the old works still turn. The Drummer beats time for them.
lore.tribalpower.spirit.shallows.3: Salt keeps. That is why the drowned things do not rot, and do not rest.
lore.tribalpower.spirit.steppe.1: The herd ran through here when the ground fell. Some of it is still running.
lore.tribalpower.spirit.steppe.2: The Pad-keepers carried this ground a basket at a time. Every stone on the steppe was once in someone's hands.
lore.tribalpower.spirit.steppe.3: The pad that was lost is not lost. It is only trampled. Quiet feet could bring it back.
lore.tribalpower.spirit.highlands.1: The wind off the highlands was a song once. The Storm Roc has been singing it wrong ever since.
lore.tribalpower.spirit.highlands.2: Boots first. Then the bridge. Then the courage. The Edge-walkers built every bridge you will cross up here.
lore.tribalpower.spirit.highlands.3: The Drum Circle stands where the Loom last agreed. Listen at night; the stones still keep the count.

lore.tribalpower.chronicle.0.title: The Old Sky
lore.tribalpower.chronicle.0.text: Before the March there was one sky and one ground under it, and nine peoples who did not agree on anything except that the ground should stay where it was. That was the first agreement, and for a long time it was enough.
lore.tribalpower.chronicle.1.title: The Nine Voices
lore.tribalpower.chronicle.1.text: Earth to hold, Fire to warm, Water to carry, Air to lift, Spirit to ask, and the Loom to bind the five. Six voices, nine peoples: three of them shared. The sharing was where the arguing started.
lore.tribalpower.chronicle.2.title: The Loom Woven
lore.tribalpower.chronicle.2.text: The Loom-stitchers found that nine threads pulled against each other would hold a weight none could hold alone. They stitched the ground to the sky with it. Every camp sang its thread. The Loom held for nine generations.
lore.tribalpower.chronicle.3.title: The Cut
lore.tribalpower.chronicle.3.text: No one remembers who stopped singing first. The Seal-carvers say a seal was carved as a demand. The Drumhearts say the beat was dropped. The Pattern-weavers say the pattern was changed without asking. All of them are right, which is the trouble.
lore.tribalpower.chronicle.4.title: The Fall
lore.tribalpower.chronicle.4.text: When one thread lets go, the other eight hold for a breath, and then they tear. The ground fell away from the sky in pieces. What did not fall drifted. What drifted is the March.
lore.tribalpower.chronicle.5.title: The Carrying
lore.tribalpower.chronicle.5.text: The Pad-keepers did not run. They picked the ground up, a basket at a time, and set a hearth on every pad they saved. The others laughed, and then they came and sat by the fires.
lore.tribalpower.chronicle.6.title: The Camps
lore.tribalpower.chronicle.6.text: Nine camps on nine pads, each singing one thread into a Loom that was no longer there. Habit, the Edge-walkers called it. Hope, the Rootbinders said. The Grit-singers said it was the same thing said twice.
lore.tribalpower.chronicle.7.title: The Unsung
lore.tribalpower.chronicle.7.text: The ninth thread would not agree even to fall. It hangs at the end of the March in a circle of stones, hollow, keeping a beat no one else can hear. The Loom-stitchers say it is waiting. They do not say for what.
lore.tribalpower.chronicle.8.title: Ash
lore.tribalpower.chronicle.8.text: The Ember Wastes were the Drumhearts' forest. It burned in the fall and never stopped. Something under the slag took up the beat when the drummers fled, and it has kept a wrong time ever since.
lore.tribalpower.chronicle.9.title: Fen
lore.tribalpower.chronicle.9.text: The Reed Fen is the Rootbinders' rope-work drowned. Every reed is a knot they tied to hold the ground; the water came anyway. One of them held on past the end. She is still holding.
lore.tribalpower.chronicle.10.title: Cairns
lore.tribalpower.chronicle.10.text: The Snow Fields are the Colony-keepers' meadows under a winter that came with the fall and stayed. The hives sleep under the cairns. The cold learned their hum and made something of its own with it.
lore.tribalpower.chronicle.11.title: Crystal
lore.tribalpower.chronicle.11.text: The Crystal Fields grew where the Grit-singers' meshes fell singing. The stone remembered the pitch and grew toward it. Most of the field is in tune. The part that is not has a long body and a longer memory.
lore.tribalpower.chronicle.12.title: The Gate
lore.tribalpower.chronicle.12.text: Glimmer Ridge is the Seal-carvers' vault, sealed from the inside on the day of the fall. What they shut in there was asked to stay, politely. It has been feeding on the asking ever since.
lore.tribalpower.chronicle.13.title: Tide
lore.tribalpower.chronicle.13.text: The Shallows are the Pattern-weavers' works, drowned to the waist and still turning. The tide keeps their pattern beat for beat. The Drummer who keeps it has forgotten there were ever weavers.
lore.tribalpower.chronicle.14.title: Steppe
lore.tribalpower.chronicle.14.text: The Steppe is the pad the Pad-keepers could not carry: too big, and the herd was on it when it fell. The herd never stopped running. Quiet feet could bring the pad back; loud ones join the stampede.
lore.tribalpower.chronicle.15.title: The Roost
lore.tribalpower.chronicle.15.text: The Highlands are the Edge-walkers' bridges, the last ground before the edge. The wind off the edge was a song once. What nests in it now sings the same song backwards and throws walkers to hear them land.

guide.tribalpower.journey.root: Pick up a Spirit Shard: dig for Echo Ore, or take one from a dawn stag's shed velvet.
guide.tribalpower.first_camp: Set down a Tribal Hearth and light it. That is a camp; everything else grows round it.
guide.tribalpower.journey.hum: Build a Pulse Resonator and feed it a shard. The hum is the camp's first power.
guide.tribalpower.journey.shatter: Raise an Echo Shatter station and break shards into grit.
guide.tribalpower.journey.attune: Raise an Echo Attune station with a Fire totem beside it and cook grit into Attuned Echo.
guide.tribalpower.journey.bind: Raise an Echo Bind station and bind Attuned Echo into Bound Echo.
guide.tribalpower.journey.manifest: Raise an Echo Manifest station and make your first Manifested Core.
guide.tribalpower.journey.core: Craft a Resonant Core. It is what every strong thing in the camp is built on.
guide.tribalpower.journey.staff: Craft a Spirit Staff and give it a voice with a totem.
guide.tribalpower.journey.ritual: Draw a rite circle: a brazier, four pedestals on the diagonals, chalk between. Seat a seal.
guide.tribalpower.first_rite: Perform a rite at your circle with a rite tablet. Rain Calling is the easiest to start with.
guide.tribalpower.journey.march: Build a Gate Drum, play its rhythm, and step through into the March.
guide.tribalpower.march.ancestor_hall: Find the Ancestor Hall on the March highlands and read what its gallery keeps.
guide.tribalpower.tribes.offering: Find a tribe's camp and lay an offering on its hearth. Bread and dirt please the Pad-keepers.
guide.tribalpower.tribes.friend: Keep offering, take their requests, trade. Friend standing opens the Elder's story.
guide.tribalpower.tribes.first_story: Ask an Elder to tell you their story, and follow it to its trial at a guardian's ground.
guide.tribalpower.march.drum_remembers: Play the four-beat on the Silent Drum in the Drum Circle and still The Unsung.
guide.tribalpower.tribes.all_stories: Finish every tribe's story: nine relics, nine guardians faced.
guide.tribalpower.march.ninth_agreement: Craft the Ninth Agreement tablet from the eight cores and an Unsung Heart, and perform it in a Loom circle with all nine relics on you.
guide.tribalpower.done: The Loom agrees. The March is yours to keep; the Chronicle, the festivals and the guardians' grounds wait for whenever you want them.

dialogue.tribalpower.soil.drummer: Slow beat today. The pads like a slow beat; it settles them.
dialogue.tribalpower.soil.hunter: Nothing hunts a pad-keeper who stays on the pad. Stay on the pad.
dialogue.tribalpower.soil.weaver: Baskets. Always baskets. You cannot carry ground in your hands.
dialogue.tribalpower.stone.drummer: I keep the mesh's time. It would sift itself off the hill otherwise.
dialogue.tribalpower.stone.hunter: Ore does not run. Everything else on this hill does, and I see to it.
dialogue.tribalpower.stone.weaver: I weave the mesh. Every strand is a note. Do not touch it while it sings.
dialogue.tribalpower.sprout.drummer: The reeds grow to the drum. Faster beat, taller reed. Do not tell the Elder.
dialogue.tribalpower.sprout.hunter: Things come up out of the fen at night. I put them back.
dialogue.tribalpower.sprout.weaver: Rope, hedge, net, rope. Every knot we tie holds a little ground.
dialogue.tribalpower.claw.drummer: The drum tells the walkers when to jump. Miss the beat and you miss the bridge.
dialogue.tribalpower.claw.hunter: I walk the edge so the camp does not have to. Do not follow me.
dialogue.tribalpower.claw.weaver: Boots. I make the boots. Nobody thanks the boots until the bridge is gone.
dialogue.tribalpower.spark.drummer: One beat. Just the one. Everything else is that beat, faster or slower.
dialogue.tribalpower.spark.hunter: I hunt on the off-beat. The dark cannot count.
dialogue.tribalpower.spark.weaver: Drum skins, drum cords, drum frames. A camp of drums needs someone who does not drum.
dialogue.tribalpower.clock.drummer: I keep the pattern's clock. The machines do not know the drum is there. That is the point.
dialogue.tribalpower.clock.hunter: Variables come out of the dark. I remove them.
dialogue.tribalpower.clock.weaver: Every belt and wire in this camp was laid to a pattern. Do not move anything.
dialogue.tribalpower.swarm.drummer: The hive keeps its own beat. I keep ours near enough that it does not mind.
dialogue.tribalpower.swarm.hunter: What hunts the hives does not hunt them twice.
dialogue.tribalpower.swarm.weaver: Wax, comb, cloth. The bees give, we shape. Good terms.
dialogue.tribalpower.sigil.drummer: A rite has a beat under it. Someone has to keep it while the Elder carves.
dialogue.tribalpower.sigil.hunter: Spirit that is not asked politely gets asked otherwise. That is my work.
dialogue.tribalpower.sigil.weaver: I weave the cloth the seals are carried in. Spirit will not sit on bare stone.
dialogue.tribalpower.spindle.drummer: Nine beats, one measure. The Loom's own time. Nobody else can hear it.
dialogue.tribalpower.spindle.hunter: I hunt for thread. The dark is full of it, if you know where to pull.
dialogue.tribalpower.spindle.weaver: Every camp sends me a thread. I stitch them. Most of the time they stay stitched.
message.tribalpower.guardian_altar.warde: Something wards this ground. The guardian will not rise here.
message.tribalpower.silent_drum.warded: Something wards the circle. The Unsung will not rise here.
message.tribalpower.request.spent: The %s have no more work for you today.
dialogue.tribalpower.soil.request.spent: That is enough for one day. Even the pads rest. Come back tomorrow.
dialogue.tribalpower.stone.request.spent: Enough. The mesh has to be re-tuned after all that. Tomorrow.
dialogue.tribalpower.sprout.request.spen: Roots grow overnight, not all at once. Tomorrow.
dialogue.tribalpower.claw.request.spent: Rest. A tired walker is a short walker. Tomorrow.
dialogue.tribalpower.spark.request.spent: Even a drum stops. Tomorrow, on the beat.
dialogue.tribalpower.clock.request.spent: The pattern allows three. Tomorrow it allows three more.
dialogue.tribalpower.swarm.request.spent: The hive rests at dusk. So do we. Tomorrow.
dialogue.tribalpower.sigil.request.spent: Ask too much of spirit in one day and it stops answering. Tomorrow.
dialogue.tribalpower.spindle.request.spe: A thread pulled all day snaps. Tomorrow.
